verified_title_publisher: PLOS ONE, Bangladesh ART adherence 15 qualitative PLHIV interviews
supported_finding: Workplace firing after HIV status disclosure and discriminatory health-provider treatment are in Discrimination subsection
correspondence_to_theme: Q01 direct employment dismissal; Q02 only clinical/provider denial, not administrative reception booking
limitations: HIV stigma true; no evidence fictional clerk or hiring case happened

verified_title_publisher: Mahmud et al. Knowledge and attitudes toward TB among social media users in Bangladesh
supported_finding: 648/1180 online respondents (54.92%) unwilling to work with someone previously treated for TB
correspondence_to_theme: Q03 direct attitude toward formerly treated TB, observational self-report only
limitations: Not a nationally representative face-to-face employer decision

verified_title_publisher: Ahsan et al. Assessment of disability of leprosy in Bangladesh
supported_finding: Facility-based 176 people studied, high disability burden, no separate cured-without-visible-impairment effect
correspondence_to_theme: Q04 insufficient to isolate disease history independently of physical disability
limitations: Correction 2026-10-16 changes study sites; do not derive fiction as recorded incident

verified_title_publisher: Ahsan et al. Correction to the leprosy disability study
supported_finding: Corrected hospital/study site list in methodology, not a new causal estimate of stigma
correspondence_to_theme: Q04 correction confirmed; study access and scope limited
limitations: Correction not replacement evidence for social discrimination mechanism

verified_title_publisher: Rashid et al. Comparative stigma among COVID-19 survivors, BMC Infectious Diseases
supported_finding: Interviews with 22 Bangladeshi survivors during 2020 and 2022-2023 documented fear/stigma/discrimination
correspondence_to_theme: Q05 direct survivor stigma historical context
limitations: Survivor experience not validation of specified volunteer decisions

verified_title_publisher: Hossain et al. Thalassemia attitudes among Bangladesh college students, Orphanet
supported_finding: 1578 Jamalpur students; of 521 familiar, about 40% unsure or unwilling to befriend a patient
correspondence_to_theme: Q06 direct friendship attitude, not actual club gatekeeping
limitations: Do not treat hereditary thalassemia as contagious

verified_title_publisher: Hossain et al. Parental perspective of thalassemia in Bangladesh, Orphanet
supported_finding: Bangladesh parents reported psychosocial burden, care barriers and perception about thalassemia
correspondence_to_theme: Q06 secondary contextual support for family/care burden, not specific student club inclusion
limitations: No direct observed student discrimination under identical conditions

verified_title_publisher: Sarker et al. Arsenicosis perception/social implications Bangladesh
supported_finding: 150 arsenicosis respondents; 32% perceived neighbors disliked participation in social activities
correspondence_to_theme: Q07 partial for diagnosis-only exclusion; visible skin findings confound
limitations: Perceived dislike, not observed uniformly nondisabled applicant rejection

verified_title_publisher: Khan et al. Perceived stigma epilepsy adolescents Dhaka
supported_finding: 206 adolescents tertiary hospital; 33% high perceived stigma and reported discrimination
correspondence_to_theme: Q08 indirect to editor/writing group selection; clinical seizure frequency associated with stigma
limitations: No legal or clinical assumption about driving/machinery; fictional tasks desk-based

verified_title_publisher: Sultana. Awareness and psychosocial support breast cancer Dhaka 240 patients
supported_finding: 240 women 2014-2017 CMH Dhaka; 75% reported community negligence, plus family difficulties
correspondence_to_theme: Q09 partial since active patients not verified completed-treatment survivors
limitations: Do not generalize to all women; body-image/physical health confounds

verified_title_publisher: Hamid and Roy. Breast cancer sociocultural barriers Bangladesh and West Bengal
supported_finding: Interview/mixed qualitative barriers to awareness, culturally connected Bangladesh+Indian West Bengal populations
correspondence_to_theme: Q09 contextual cross-border mechanisms, not complete-treatment community roles
limitations: Mixed-country source cannot count as exclusively Bangladeshi cohort

verified_title_publisher: Sakil et al. Hepatitis B university-student survey Gopalganj Bangladesh
supported_finding: 440 students; 266/440 (60.45%) perceived discrimination; 199/440 (45.23%) uncomfortable with HBV patients
correspondence_to_theme: Q10 direct stigma/discomfort, not observed online study-group exclusions
limitations: Non-exposure collaboration only; HBV transmission concern should not be exaggerated
